answer: A stake-bonded trust graph resists Sybil attacks. Every agent is a vertex that must lock a refundable deposit and earn a vouch from an established agent before transacting. A cluster of fresh accounts forms a nebula: many vertices, but no bridge edge connects them to the trusted core, so their combined weight stays near zero. Forging a bridge costs money or reputation, since the voucher forfeits part of its deposit if its vouchee misbehaves. An attacker must therefore pay per fake identity and buy trust links for each one, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousandfold while each fake earns little.
